title: Q0 fact tf32_off: checker read the image's env-var DEFAULT instead of the effective TF32 state
written_utc_note: Written BEFORE J1_diag_decision_r2.json was produced; see file mtimes and deviation_DEV-001_outcome.json.

trigger.processes_failing: all 8 (A0-A3, NC0-NC3), independent of arm, lr or outcome
trigger.every_other_fact_and_check: true / passed; all 4 negative controls REJECTED

root_cause: The ACP image exports TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1 (recorded in every J1 provenance.json).
earthdelta.fs_protocol.tf32_is_off additionally required that variable to be unset/'0', on the incorrect belief that it FORCES TF32.

In the certified torch 2.3.1 the variable appears only as the member initializer of Context::float32_matmul_precision (ATen/Context.h); Context::allowTF32CuBLAS() returns float32_matmul_precision != HIGHEST (ATen/Context.cpp v2.3.1).
r2_fs_bank_train.py (and s0_gate.py) set torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False and cudnn.allow_tf32=False at import, before any CUDA work, which resets the precision to HIGHEST: TF32 is OFF.
The J1 provenance records the effective getters cuda_matmul_allow_tf32=False and cudnn_allow_tf32=False.
evidence: PyTorch v2.3.1 source: ATen/Context.h member initializer `float32_matmul_precision = check_env("TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE") == true ? HIGH : HIGHEST`; Context::allowTF32CuBLAS() reads only that member.
Executor reproduction, overlay torch 2.3.1+cu121, env=1: after the explicit setters, getter False and precision 'highest'.
Coordinator independent reproduction, overlay torch 2.3.1+cu121, env=1: BEFORE setters allow_tf32=True / precision 'high'; AFTER setters allow_tf32=False, cudnn False, precision 'highest'.
s0_gate.py lines 125-126 issue the same explicit setters, so S0 and the Fs processes ran in the same effective FP32 (TF32-off) mode.

fix.change_1: tf32_is_off: TF32 off iff the EFFECTIVE recorded getters cuda_matmul_allow_tf32 and cudnn_allow_tf32 are both False and, when recorded, float32_matmul_precision == 'highest'. The env variable is still recorded but no longer decisive.
fix.change_2: collect_provenance records torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() (from J2 on) as an independent cross-check.
fix.tests: tests/test_fs_quality_gate.py: env='1' + explicit setters -> off; env='1' without setters -> NOT off (live fresh-interpreter subprocess, both directions); getter True / precision 'high' -> NOT off. Diff: plans/plan_v4_0923/run_20260923T192759Z_fp03_fs/forensics/DEV-001_tests.diff

why_not_post_hoc: The bug is in a Q0 infrastructure/validity fact-checker, not in any Q1-Q6 scientific threshold, the experimental argv, or candidate selection; Q0 failures are pre-registered validity failures, categorically separate from scientific verdicts (confirmed interpretation (b)).
It failed identically for all 8 processes regardless of arm, lr or outcome, so it cannot be outcome-correlated.
It was root-caused at the PyTorch source level and reproduced empirically by both executor and coordinator.
The original STOP decision stays on disk untouched; the re-decision is a new file.
approval: Coordinator approved option (A) in writing before J1_diag_decision_r2.json was produced; options (B) protocol v2 and (C) exporting the env var in J2's argv were rejected.
action: Re-run the J1 diag decision with the J1-snapshot decider + only this fs_protocol.py change (the working tree differs from the J1 snapshot only in fs_protocol.py and tests/test_fs_quality_gate.py), writing decisions/J1_diag_decision_r2.json. Submit J2 with the frozen, unchanged argv only if r2 is PASS. J2's snapshot will carry the fixed fs_protocol.py; this is the only source drift from source_at_preregistration.
why_a_separate_file: forensics/historical_fs_forensics.json is pinned by SHA-256 in the frozen protocol (inputs.forensics); editing it would break that binding, so deviations are recorded in new files beside it.
